dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: How's it going? Have you found all the Future Stars?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not yet.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Oh... Did you not know how to use "Banu's Wisdom"? It's really simple, just do as the manual says.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's a manual?

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Of course! Wait, did you not see one? Oh no, I must've forgotten to bring it...

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: But it's okay. Just put "Banu's Wisdom" on the ground and it will automatically point to where the Future Stars are. All you need to do is to follow its guidance.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Remember, after it runs for a while, it will need to rest a bit before it can point you to the location of the Future Stars again.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Where's the manual?

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: I put it with "Banu's Wisdom." Wait, did you not see one? Oh no, I must've forgotten to bring it from home...

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: But it's okay. Just put "Banu's Wisdom" on the ground and it will automatically point to where the Future Stars are. All you need to do is to follow its guidance.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Remember, after it runs for a while, it will need to rest a bit before it can point you to the location of the Future Stars again.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We have.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: See? I'm not lying and the Future Stars are all real! After all, Shalmar buried them himself.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: As an adult, he may not be the most reliable, if at all. But he'd never lie to me. I believe him.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: I've marked the location of the Future Stars on the map. Just follow that map and you should be able to find them all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd like to have a chat.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Ah, this I can really relate to. It gets boring easier than you'd believe when you are out in the wild all by yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: When I was at home, I had so many things to do every day. Apart from all the housework, I had to cook meals for Shalmar with Apple, or else he'd have nothing to eat and starve.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Those were some busy days, but I never felt bored. But now, I'm away from home and all by myself, so I understand how you feel completely.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Shalmar...

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: You want to know about Shalmar? Well, Shalmar is Shalmar, can't cook meals, can't sweep floors, just another terrible adult.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: He's either writing reports in his study at home, or working at the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: I remember he's one of those Spantamad researchers. But his job is so vastly different from that of those amazing traveling scholars who are always on the road.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: He told me that he just sorts out old stuff in a dark warehouse every day, which isn't cool at all. And no one would play with him and that's just sad.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: So whenever he's bored, I hang out with him, and we come up with all kinds of settings. Someone's got to keep him company and play with him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Settings?

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Yes, settings. You looked as confused as when we were talking about the setting of the Future Stars just now. Are you unfamiliar with settings?

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: I can teach you how to come up with them. So next time, when you get bored, you can create your own settings just for fun.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Shalmar said settings are just sets of rules. Many rules are created by others, but you can also create your own rules. And that's fun!

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: For example, Shalmar would take back old items that the Akademiya had intended to get rid of. We would come up with a setting for each item and all of a sudden, they became new and useful.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Shalmar and I came up with the setting of the Future Stars together. They used to be called Parvo Cores. I mean, "Future Star" is just a much better name than that, right?

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: But soon, I'll be studying at the Akademiya and have little time to hang out with Shalmar anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About 50 Things Every Traveling Scholar Should Know...

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: You mean the book I lent you? Don't worry about it, I've got a few more copies in my pack and a good pile at home.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: They've printed too many copies, so the editor just gave the rest to us. After all, Shalmar wrote the book.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: I've been preparing to become a traveling scholar, so I've read that book many times, to the point where I can recite most of it. So it's fine to lend it to others.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Although, the copy I lent to you only has a few pages left. Save for the map, I've used most of the pages to light fires...

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: If you want to give it a read, I can lend you an intact copy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why do you want to become a traveling scholar?

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Hmmm... Because traveling scholars can travel the world and that's fun!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Adventurers can also travel the world.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: But traveling scholars can contribute more, y'know. I often heard those adults at the Citadel of Regzar complain about those adventurers trapping themselves in the desert and that they had to send people to rescue them.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: While traveling scholars get to study abroad with their certificates in different countries. Isn't that awesome? And they usually bring tons of useful reports back to the Akademiya as well.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: While you were searching for the Future Stars, I wasn't slacking off here. I've been writing my traveling report and I'm halfway through it already.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Anyway... I'd most like to become a traveling scholar. But if I can't be that, I'll consider becoming an adventurer as you suggested.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Apple...

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Do you want to know her? I can introduce you to Apple for sure!

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Apple is my best friend. When I was little, mom brought her back home. She used to carry me on her back and walk me around. She'd help me cook too!

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Whenever we were running short of fish and meat back home, she would go out and buy some fresh fish and meat for me.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Apple is the best! With her by my side, no one dares to bully me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Bye.

dialogues.speaker: Banu
dialogues.text: Are you going now? Okay. Come back to me when you find all the Future Stars!
